text:
[LTIM.2.8.3] **The wall clock** reads UTC nanoseconds since the Unix epoch.
It **may** jump forward or move backward between two samples — a host clock
set by an operator or stepped by time synchronisation does both. It drives
`now()` ([LTIM.2.1]) and the `ts` the engine fills ([LFAC.9.2]), and nothing
else.

A condition reading `now()` observes the wall clock as it is: a gate such as a
comparison of `now()` against a fixed instant can become false again when the
wall clock moves backward across the instant, and true again when it moves
forward ([LTIM.2.5.1]). An author who needs a gate that stays open once opened
measures elapsed time on the monotonic clock instead — `dwell`, `within`, or a
difference of `monotonic_ns()` readings.

**The wall clock may have no value**: a mock clock before the test sets it
([NLFC.5.4]), or a live clock on a host that supplies no wall-clock source.
A `now()` read while it has none, or the engine filling a `ts` from it
([LFAC.9.2]), is a `ComputationError` of kind `DOMAIN` ([LERR.1.4.10]), and
the engine continues. In a rule's activation (a `now()` read, an `emit` or a
`publish`) the activation is abandoned and the rule does not fire. For an
`initial` block's fact ([LGRA.24.3]) the fact is not placed. Once the wall
clock has a value, `now()` reads it.

idris.name: lcrs_6_2_1__wall_called
idris.note: The wall step: Rete/NetworkWall.idr's; the call trackers stand.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__second_edge_refires
idris.note: 'A gate such as a comparison of `now()` against a fixed instant can become false again ... and true again': the window that shuts and reopens fires once per opening, `[1, 0, 1, 0]`, computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__reads_wall
idris.note: 'It drives `now()` ... and nothing else': the wall clock is observed through the `now()` leaf alone, which this criterion is the test for.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__counts_ignore_wall
idris.note: However the wall clock is stepped, a history's counts under monotonic gates are the counts it had.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__remap_wall
idris.note: 'May jump forward or move backward between two samples': a history's wall samples rewritten by any function at all.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__wall_gate_reopens
idris.note: 'A gate such as a comparison of `now()` against a fixed instant can become false again when the wall clock moves backward across the instant, and true again when it moves forward': `[1, 0, 1, 0]` over a wall that goes 1, 2, 1, 2, computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__wall_start
idris.note: The one rule under the wall window at (0, 0). A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__wall_window
idris.note: 'It drives `now()`': a gate on `now()` reads the wall sample as it is. A fixture.

idris.name: Ltim_2_8_3__step
idris.note: A wall step among a fixture's steps: the clause's 'may jump forward or move backward between two samples', as a step the engine is driven with. A fixture.

idris.name: iret_12_2__successor_rules
idris.note: `fresh` reads the wall; the two rules beside it do not. A fixture.

idris.name: ldet_5_8__late_gate
idris.note: A gate on the wall sample against a fixed instant. A fixture.

idris.name: llog_3_11_1__fresh_rule
idris.note: A rule whose condition reads the wall and whose RHS justifies a logical fact. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__now_window
idris.note: A gate comparing `now()` with fixed instants, which can be false and then true again. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__window_second_edge_refires_timed
idris.note: 'True again when it moves forward': the window reopens at 3 on an advancing wall, a second edge. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__wall_step_moves_no_monotonic_pump
idris.note: However the wall clock is stepped -- 'forward or backward' -- a monotonic `where` fires as it would have: the wall step is observed by `now()` and by nothing else, on this engine by theorem.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_2__wall_steps_move_no_dwell_timed
idris.note: 'An author who needs a gate that stays open once opened measures elapsed time on the monotonic clock instead -- `dwell`': under two wall steps, once. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__at_one
idris.note: `now() == 1`: a gate on the wall clock against a fixed instant, logical/LTIM.2.8.3_wall_gate_reopens's `at_one` in the witnesses' units. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__no_wall_step_is_the_timed_run
idris.note: With no wall step the wall sample is never moved, and the run is Rete/NetworkTimed.idr's with the wall held: what every fixture whose lowering writes no wall step runs.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__now_leaf
idris.note: `now()` in a `where`: the clock leaf that reads the wall sample. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__now_leaf_reads_the_wall
idris.note: THE `now()` LEAF READS THE WALL SAMPLE: under any sample, stamp table and token, the substitution replaces it by the wall component as an Int. 'It drives `now()`'. A TRANSCRIPTION of Rete/NetworkTimed.idr's `ltim_2_4_1__read_at`'s first clause, said so: it fails if the leaf is changed to read the monotonic sample or a stamp and refutes nothing else.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__now_test_is_not_monotonic
idris.note: A `now()` TEST IS NOT A MONOTONIC GATE: the timed test of `now() == 1` admits the Ping at the sample (0, 1) and refuses it at (0, 2), both computed, so no proof that it answers alike at two wall samples exists. C2's hypothesis is not inhabited by a `where` that reads the wall, and nothing in this module says a wall step leaves such a rule alone: what the clause's second paragraph allows, and `wall_gate_reopens_timed` executes.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__ping
idris.note: The one Ping the wall witnesses match: kind 0, key 1, no payload. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__pump_proj
idris.note: A pump's result with its state projected: the gated state, the halt and the trace. By a triple pattern, so that it reduces on a named result; what C2 compares through.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__run_steps_wall
idris.note: A FIXTURE'S STEPS on the timed engine with the wall, in its cadence: a wall step moves the wall sample; every other step is Rete/NetworkTimed.idr's; every pump's verdicts collected. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__verdicts_of
idris.note: THE VERDICTS OF A SCHEDULE WITH THE WALL from the loaded network: one list per pump. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__wall_gate_reopens_timed
idris.note: C3b ON THIS ENGINE. A GATE ON THE WALL CLOCK CAN REOPEN: the Ping asserted at (0, 0) under `now() == 1`; an advance to 1 and a pump fire; an advance to 2 and a pump find the gate shut, which ends the match; a tick to 3 with the wall stepped BACK to 1 and a pump find it open again, a new match, and fire; an advance to 4 and a pump fire nothing -- logical/LTIM.2.8.3_wall_gate_reopens's shape, Rete/NetworkTwoClocks.idr's `ltim_2_8_3__wall_gate_reopens` on the Idris model's engine through its wall steps. 'Can become false again when the wall clock moves backward across the instant, and true again when it moves forward.' Executed: `[[(0, True)], [], [(0, True)], []]`.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__wall_set_keeps_stamps
idris.note: THE WALL STEP KEEPS THE STAMPS: `dwell` measures from the entry stamp, and a wall step enters no fact; the stamp table after it is the one before, for every instant and state. A transcription.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__wall_set_projects
idris.note: THE WALL STEP PROJECTS TO THE IDENTITY: the gated state under the timed state -- the clocked net with its clock, deadlines and rows, and the trackers -- is what it was, for every instant and state. A TRANSCRIPTION of the definition, said so: it fails if the step is changed to touch the net or the trackers and refutes nothing else.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__wall_set_sets_the_wall
idris.note: AND SETS THE WALL: to the instant named, whatever it was, for every instant and state. A transcription.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__wall_set_timed
idris.note: THE WALL STEP: the wall sample set alone, to any instant, earlier or later; the clocked net, the stamps and the trackers stand. 'May jump forward or move backward between two samples', as the engine receives it; not a sample ([NTST.3.3]), the next pump reads what it left.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__wm_after
idris.note: THE WORKING MEMORY after a schedule with the wall from the loaded network. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__stepped_back
idris.note: A clock source whose wall clock goes BACK: (1, 9) and then (2, 4). A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_3__wall_moves_a_now_gate
idris.note: 'A gate such as a comparison of `now()` against a fixed instant can become false again when the wall clock moves backward across the instant': `now() > 5`, true at (3, 6), false at (3, 4). Computed.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_5__wall_goes_back_on_replay
idris.note: 'May jump forward or move backward between two samples': a wall clock that went back is replayed as it went, (1, 9) and then (2, 4).
